children.value: > Fact From Story If the court finds that social media companies don’t have a First Amendment right to curate the kinds of content that they allow, social platforms could look very different, at least in states that are trying to limit their moderation powers.

> > Fact From Story The question here is: Do social media companies have a First Amendment protected right to exercise what you might call editorial judgment — or what you also might call content moderation — in sorting out what expression does and does not appear on the platforms that they own? | Deduced Fact
> > > > Fact From Story “These cases are about the First Amendment and how the First Amendment applies to social media companies. | Deduced Fact
> > > > Commonsense Knowledge The First Amendment protects freedom of speech. | Commonsense Knowledge
> > Commonsense Knowledge Content moderation is how social media companies decide what content is allowed on their platforms. | Commonsense Knowledge

> Fact From Story After years of slow progress on misinformation — and worrisome backsliding on platforms like Elon Musk’s X — the Supreme Court’s decision could upend that process, sowing chaos online in the process.

> > Fact From Story “Thanks to the First Amendment, Florida and Texas cannot force websites or social media apps to host hateful content, misinformation and spam, as their deeply misguided laws would require,”
> > > Fact From Story In Texas, the law told social media companies that they could no longer remove or demonetize content based on the “viewpoint represented in the user’s expression.”

> > > Fact From Story The two laws — HB 20 in Texas and SB 7072 in Florida — are very similar in their origins and intentions, but diverge slightly in how they seek to restrict social media platforms.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Laws can have a significant impact on how social media companies operate.
> > Commonsense Knowledge The First Amendment protects websites from being forced to host content they don't want to.
> Commonsense Knowledge The Supreme Court can make impactful decisions.
